ai.title: Fix flaky e2e CLI tests
ai.summary: Increased timeout to 8s and added exit listener in `e2e-cli.test.ts`. Fixes flakiness from slow CI startup. Scope: CLI test suite.

eli5.text: You're a developer who runs automated tests for the command-line tool. Tests that launch the tool with the --agent flag have been randomly failing on slow continuous-integration machines because they shut down before the tool finished starting up. The test now waits longer (up to 8 seconds) and treats a process that is still alive after that wait as a successful startup, while also catching an early exit as a failure. If you ran these end-to-end CLI tests today you would notice they no longer time out and report false failures on slower machines. This change is live today and affects only the CLI test suite, so you would notice it only when running those tests.

ai.title: Fix message context loss on CLI response cancellation
ai.summary: Moved `finalizeQueueState` from the abort listener in `cli/src/hooks/helpers/send-message.ts` to `handleRunCompletion` to prevent race conditions where users could send new messages before the cancelled run's state was saved. This ensures the chain lock remains held until `client.run()` resolves, preserving message history integrity. Scope covers CLI streaming hooks and associated SDK cancellation tests.

eli5.text: If you cancel a reply while the assistant is still typing in the CLI, your message history stays intact instead of getting lost. Previously, the system released its lock too early during cancellation, letting new messages in before the previous state was saved. Now the lock stays held until the cancelled response fully completes, so the assistant can't accidentally start a new reply with stale context. This is live today for anyone using the CLI streaming feature.

ai.title: evalbuff direct LLM API and trivial commit filtering
ai.summary: evalbuff package replaces `claude` CLI spawning with direct `@ai-sdk/anthropic` API calls in `evalbuff/src/llm.ts`, removing process overhead and context pollution. `commit-task-generator.ts` adds `isTrivialCommit` logic to skip version bumps and changelog updates, saving agent invocations. Judge aggregation switches to averaging scores across reviewers to neutralize model-specific biases. New `base2-free-evals.ts` agent definition supports the free evals orchestrator.

eli5.text: An automated helper that checks how well code fixes work has been sped up and made fairer. It now talks to the AI model directly instead of launching a separate program each time, which removes wasted overhead. When summarizing results from multiple reviewers, it now averages the scores instead of picking the middle one, since different AI models have a habit of rating things consistently higher or lower than others. It also ignores boring commits like version bumps and dependency updates, so it won't waste time running checks on changes that don't need human-like review.

ai.title: Agent grid splits large agents onto full-width lines
ai.summary: Consecutive small agents share a `GridLayout` row while each large agent gets its own full-width line. `block-processor.ts` adds `splitByAgentSize` and `splitAgentsBySize` using `shouldCollapseByDefault` to partition items. `agent-block-grid.tsx` and `message-with-agents.tsx` map these subgroups into stacked `GridLayout` instances inside a column `box`. Small agents collapse by default and pack together; large agents render at full terminal width.

eli5.text: When you run several agents in the CLI, the small ones now crowd together on a single line while each big agent takes up the full width of the terminal. Behind the scenes, the grid logic separates agents by size before drawing them: small agents (which collapse by default) are packed into shared rows, and large agents are placed each on their own full-width line. If you are watching an agent session today, you will see this tighter packing right away when a mix of small and large agents appear together.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to use Fireworks, it now gives the tool instructions in a stricter, more precise format. This only affects requests sent to the Fireworks service and prevents the assistant from making up incorrect tool calls. You wouldn’t notice anything different in how the assistant responds, but behind the scenes the requests are more reliable.

ai.title: coerceToArray wraps zod array schemas in tool params
ai.summary: Added `coerceToArray` preprocess wrapper to array fields in `ask-user`, `propose-str-replace`, `read-files`, `read-subtree`, `spawn-agents`, `str-replace`, and `suggest-followups`. Handles upstream models emitting single objects instead of arrays for tool arguments. Scope limited to `common/src/tools/params/tool/` schemas.

eli5.text: You may have noticed that when an AI assistant hands back a list of choices or files to read, it used to break if a single item was returned instead of a proper list. That happened because some of the assistants behind the scenes occasionally sent back a single object where the system expected a whole list. Now, the system has been updated to automatically wrap those lone items into a list on your behalf, so the assistant correctly processes them instead of failing. This affects tools like ask-user, read-files, propose-str-replace, read-subtree, spawn-agents, str-replace, suggest-followups, and write-todos, all of which now handle single-item responses gracefully. This fix is live today and required no action on your part.

ai.title: thinker-gpt stops inheriting parent system prompt
ai.summary: Added `inheritParentSystemPrompt: false` to the `thinker-gpt` agent definition in `agents/thinker/thinker-gpt.ts`. The agent now runs with only its own instructions prompt, preventing parent system prompt leakage. Scope limited to the thinker-gpt agent config.

eli5.text: The thinker-gpt helper no longer copies over the main set of background rules that guide it, so it now follows only its own dedicated instructions. This affects anyone who relies on the thinker-gpt helper, which will behave more narrowly since it can no longer pick up extra rules from the parent setup. If you interact with it, you may notice it gives more focused answers that stick closely to its specific task description.

eli5.text: When you look at the list of AI models you can assign to an automated helper, you'll now see "Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview" available as an option. In everyday use, this means the special helper that judges how well other helpers are performing in our internal tests has quietly been switched to use this newer Gemini model, so those comparisons now run on more recent technology. You won't see anything different unless you're actually looking at the model-selection menu or reviewing the latest judge test outcomes.

ai.title: Freebuff releases version 0.0.26
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI package version increments from 0.0.25 to 0.0.26 in `cli/release/package.json`, wrapping the March 30 release train. This release bundles notable updates including a CLI stop button in the status bar, direct Anthropic API calls in evalbuff, agent grid layout improvements, and zod coerceToArray fixes for array tool params. No source code changes accompany this bump.
ai.evidence: In `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, the `version` field in the `freebuff` package manifest changed from `0.0.25` to `0.0.26`. This is a release-bump commit with no functional changes (+1/-1).

eli5.text: Version 0.0.26 makes your AI coding assistant more reliable and pleasant to use. It adds a prominent Stop button to the status bar so you can instantly halt a slow or runaway response while it is streaming, and it fixes a bug where canceling one response could accidentally let you queue up the next message before the previous work was safely saved. The built-in evaluation system now calls AI models directly instead of going through a separate command-line process, which makes test runs faster and cleaner, and it filters out pointless commits like version bumps so you get clearer quality results. Your conversation history stays intact when you cancel streaming messages, and the agent grid layout looks tidier with small quick tools grouped together while big detailed agents each get their own full-width line. You can now use newer Google Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview models when judging agent performance, and several tools handle single object inputs gracefully to prevent formatting errors.

ai.title: Cli release bumped to 1.0.636
ai.summary: The CLI release package version in `cli/release/package.json` was incremented from 1.0.635 to 1.0.636 as part of the standard release packaging workflow. This version bump accompanies the cumulative user-facing features and fixes shipped since 1.0.635, including optional GitHub OAuth environment variables, evalbuff direct LLM API calls, CLI status bar stop button, message context loss fix on cancellation, agent grid layout improvements, and Fireworks strict mode.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `1.0.635` to `1.0.636`. This is the only change in the commit, which is classified as a release-bump commit type.

eli5.text: This release adds a new AI model option, makes the chat interface easier to control, and improves the accuracy of automated coding tasks. You can now use Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview when setting up agents and judgment tasks, giving you access to a newer, more capable model for complex reasoning. A new Stop button appears in the status bar while the assistant is thinking or responding, so you can interrupt a long-running answer without losing your place in the conversation. Background code evaluation tools now filter out meaningless changes like version-number bumps, skip trivial commits, and average scores across multiple reviewers to produce fairer results. The agent display layout was also refined so smaller agents group together neatly while larger ones get full-width space, keeping your terminal workspace cleaner when multiple tools are shown.

ai.title: Tool executor error includes truncated input
ai.summary: Tool executor now appends the original tool call input to error messages. Input is JSON-stringified and truncated at 500 chars to prevent log bloat. Affects `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts` in both standard and custom tool execution paths.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to use a tool (like a calculator or a web search) and that tool call fails, you used to only see a generic error message with no context about what went wrong. Now, the error message will include the actual instruction that was sent to the tool, showing you exactly what the assistant tried to do, so you can better understand why it failed. The instruction is shown as plain text and is automatically shortened if it's very long, keeping the error messages readable while still giving helpful detail. This is live today for all users.

ai.title: Fix condition hook use in message-with-agents
ai.summary: Moved `useMemo` hook above conditional returns in `AgentChildrenGrid` within `cli/src/components/message-with-agents.tsx`. This resolves React hook rule violations where hooks were called after early returns (`agentChildren.length === 0` or `depth >= MAX_AGENT_DEPTH`). Scope limited to CLI component rendering. Ensures consistent hook execution order regardless of render path.

eli5.text: When the CLI displays a grid of agent children, it now always sets up the data needed to group those agents before deciding whether to skip rendering entirely. Previously, that grouping step happened after early exit checks, so the order of internal setup changed depending on which path ran; now the setup always runs first, keeping the rendering logic consistent. You won't see a visual difference day to day, but this prevents crashes tied to that inconsistent ordering. This is live today in the CLI component that renders agent grids.
